Have you ever found yourself pausing in a quiet moment, wondering what it really means to believe in something—or someone? Sometimes, those questions come alive when we listen to stories of people whose lives look nothing like our own.
That’s exactly the journey we’re invited to in Mitch Albom’s Have a Little Faith: a True Story. Here, we meet two men: one, a beloved rabbi facing the twilight of his years; the other, a man who’s walked the hard road from prison to the pulpit. Both are searching—wrestling with faith, forgiveness, and what it means to trust. As their paths cross, we start to see how little moments—an act of kindness, a word of hope—can echo through a community. Together, we’ll explore how faith isn’t just a comfort, but sometimes a tough call to action. We’ll look at questions of trust, redemption, and the deep desire we all share for connection and meaning. So, as the world of Have a Little Faith unfolds, let’s reflect together on the way hope, wisdom, and small everyday choices can shape not just our own lives, but the lives of those around us. Ready to begin? Let’s step into this story—and see what we just might discover about faith, community, and the meaning that ties us all together.
